lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Qunirul Haque Siddique and Abdul Barek: Chowdhury -----For the Appellant.
AJ Mohammad Ali with Md Nurul Amin -----For the Respondent Nos. 1-3, 5 and 6.
parties:
Khan Mohammad Ameer ------ Appellant
Vs.
Atiqur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Khasruzzaman J: This first appeal has been preferred by the plaintiff against the judgment and decree dated 4-7-2013 (decree signed on 8-7-20l3) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.838 of 2012 rejecting the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. The appellant as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 838 of 2012 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the respondents as defendants for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit land which is more particularly described in the schedule to the plaint.

3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that:

The suit land originally belonged to the then DIT now Rajuk. DIT leased out the suit property in favour of Motiur Rahman Mullick, son of late Abdur Rahman Mullick by standard lease agreement for land vide registered deed No. 2808 dated 13-3-1961 and handed over possession thereof to him. The said leasee Motiur Rahman Mullick constructed a two storied building on the suit plot and while peacefully possessing the same, transferred the suit plot to his brother Habibur Rahman, the father of the defendant Nos.1-5, vide registered deed No. 2522 dated 31-3-1969 and handed over possession to him. Habibur Rahman Mullick passed away on 7-4-1979 leaving behind his wife Meherunnessa, a son Atiqur Rahman, defendant Nos. 1 and 4 daughters, defendant Nos. 2-5, as his legal heirs and successors. The defendant Nos. 1-5 and their mother mutated their names in the office of the Rajuk vide memo No. RAJUK/Estate/203 dated 17-1-1989. Mrs Meherunnessa, mother of the defendant Nos. 1-5, and defendant Nos. 1-5 entered in to an agreement for sale of the suit land with the plaintiff on 7-7-1987 fixing Taka 70,00,000 as the consideration money and out of which they received a sum of Taka 15,00,000 as baina on the dale of the said agreement. Thereafter, the defendant Nos. 1-5 and their mother received a total sum of Taka 39,50,000 from the plaintiff on different dates by cash and cheque. Thus they received a total sum of Taka 54,50,000 out of the consideration money of Taka 70,00,000. Subsequently, Meherunnessa died leaving behind the said defendant Nos. 1-5 as her legal heirs and successors who entered into a2m agreement for sale vide registered deed No.11363 dated 4-8-1999 with the plaintiff acknowledging receipt of Taka 54,50,000 and on that date they also received Taka 1,00,000 and, as such, in total they, received Taka 55,50,000 with a condition for performance of the said 2nd  contract within 5 years from the date of execution. It was stated in the said agreement for sale that the period of performance of contract would be extended on consent of both the parties. The defendant Nos. 1-5 executed a power of attorney appointing Mrs Rokshana Ameer, the wife of the plaintiff, proforma defendant No. 18 as their attorney to execute sale deed in respect of the suit property on their behalf and the same was registered vide deed No. 11363 dated 4-8-1999. There were two suits being Title Suit Nos. 1 of 2000(G) and 2 of 2000(G) pending between the defendants including Rajuk and one Niyemat Ali Sheikh, Niyemat Ali Sheikh being dead his heirs and successors were substituted as defendant Nos. 7-14, both the suits were pending before the Appellate Division. For the reasons stated above, specific performance of contract with the defendant Nos. 1-5 was not possible. The defendant Nos. 1-5 insisted upon the plaintiff to enhance the price of the scheduled land and ultimately the price was fixed by enhancing Taka 2,20,00,000 from Taka 70,00,000 and on the request of the defendant Nos. 1-5, their constituted attorney defendant No. 18 executed a fresh deed of agreement for sale on 4-10-2009 fixing the price of the schedule land at Taka 2,20,00,000 and accordingly received a sum of Taka 30,00,000 from the plaintiff. Thus the defendant Nos. 1-5 received a total sum of Taka 1,00,00,000 as earnest money from the plaintiff out of total consideration money Taka 2,20,00,000. Thereafter, the defendant Nos. 1-5 insisted upon the plaintiff No.1 through their constituted attorney defendant No. 18 for payment a sum of Taka 1,19,80,000 out of the balance consideration money due to their urgent need of money. Accordingly, the plaintiff paid Taka 1,19,80,000 and on receipt of the said amount, the defendant No. 18, the constituted attorney of the defendant Nos. 1-5, executed another deed of agreement for sale on 19-11-2009 which was also registered in the office of the Gulshan Sub-registry Office. It is stated in the plaint that the defendant No. 18 requested- the defendant Nos. 1-5 to take Taka 1,49,80 from her which was lying with her and on several occasions the defendant No. 18 requested them to receive the same but they deferred it on various plea. Thus the plaintiff paid Taka;2,19,80,000 in respect of the suit plot out of total consideration money of Taka 2,20,00,000. The defendant No. 18 on 19-10-2010 filed an application to Rajuk seeking sale permission of the suit plot but the same could not be procured due to pendency of Civil Appeal Nos. 201 of 2009 and 202 of 2009 before the Appellate Division (arising out of aforesaid Title Suit Nos. 1 of 2000 and 2 of2000 respectively). In the mean time, the defendant Nos. 1-5 were trying to sell the scheduled land to others as a result, a precautionary notice was published in the "Daily Ittefaq" on 27-10-2010 drawing attention of all concern to the aforesaid two registered sale agreements between the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 1-5 and the registered power of attorney dated 4-8-1999. The defendant Nos. 1-5 on perusal of the said notice, published a notice in the 'Daily Kaler Kantha' on 2-11- 2010 stating that they had already cancelled the registered power of attorney No. 11363 dated 4-8-1999 executed in favour of the defendant No. 18 byregistered deed of revocation being No. 8427 dated 9-4-2010. The defendant No. 18 filed Title Suit No. 94 of 2011 on 27-1-2011 in the 111 Court of the Joint District Judge, Dhaka challenging the aforesaid deed of revocation of power of attorney against the defendant Nos. 1-5, which is pending before that Court. The plaintiff on search with the office of the Gulshan Sub-Registry Office, Dhaka came to know that the defendant Nos. 1-5 entered into two sale agreements in respect of the suit land being registered deed Nos. 3285 and 3291 dated 9-5-2012 with the defendant No.6. Thereafter the plaintiff obtained the certified copies of the said two sale deeds on 23-5- 2012. It is further stated in the plaint that the defendant Nos. 2-5 entered into 4 registered agreements for sale with one Mr Dulalur Rahman Sagar vide Nos. 8608 dated 4-8-2030, 9488 dated 31-8-2010, 9232 dated 24-8-2010, and 9487 dated 31-8-2010. Subsequently, the defendant Nos. 2-5.cancelled the aforesaid deeds on 9-5-2012 by 4 (four) cancellation deeds. The plaintiff apprehends from the conduct of the defendant Nos. 1-5 that defendants will sell the suit property after disposal of the Civil Appeal Nos. 201 of 1999 and 202 of 1999 pending before the Appellate Division and, as such, the plaintiff constrained to file the suit for protection of his legal rights.

4. The defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to the then DIT, now Rajuk, and the suit plot was leased out in favour of Motiur Rahman Mullick who transferred the same to his full brother Habibur Rahman, father of the defendant, Nos. 1-5, by registered sale deed. Habibur Rahman passed away leaving behind a wife. Meherunnessa, Atiqur Rahman, defendant No.1, and 4 sisters defendant Nos. 2-5. They mutated their names in the office of the Rajuk and were in possession of the suit land. Meherunnassa died leaving behind defendant Nos. 1-5 as her legal heirs and successors. Their further caseis that the defendant Nos. 1-5 did not enter into any unregistered agreement for sale of the suit land on, 7-7-1987 and registered deed of agreement for sale on 4-8-1999, 4-10-2009 and 19-11-9 or on any dates before and after those dates. They did not receive any part of the consideration money from the plaintiff as baina in respect of the suit plot. If any deed of agreement for sale of the suit plot is found in the name of defendant Nos. 1-5 as executants and plaintiff as baina receiver, that must have been forged, false, void, concocted and created documents and no right, title and interest will be created in favour of the parties on the basis of the said void documents. Their further case is that the defendant No. 18 took a power of attorney on 4-8-1999 from the defendant Nos. 1-5 by practicing fraud and undue influence and the said power of attorney was revoked by a deed of revocation being No. 8427 dated 29-7-20-10. Defendant Nos. 1-5 did not receive any sum of money through their attorney, defendant No. 18, and the said power of attorney was not duly approved by the Rajuk and, as such, defendant No. 18 filed Writ Petition No.6360 of 2010 against Rajuk in the High Court Division and Rajuk filed an affidavit-in-opposition in the said writ petition. The plaintiff with ill motive and to grab the suit land filed the instant suit on some false allegations which is barred by law, Hence the same is liable to be dismissed.

5. Defendant No. 18, power of attorney holder of defendant Nos. 1-5, by filing a written statement contested the suit stating inter alia, that the defendant Nos. 1-5 executed registered power of attorney deed No. 11364 dated 4-8-1999 in favour of her in respect of the suit land to execute sale deed. By supporting the plaintiffs case, she further stated that she entered into an agreement for sale vide registered deed No. 8779 dated 4-10-9 by enhancing the price fixed from Taka 70,00,000 to Taka 2,20,00,00 with the plaintiff. She entered another agreement for sale of the suit land with plaintiff vide registered deed dated 19-11-2009-by taking Taka 1,19,80,000 out of total consideration money Taka 2,20,00,000. Thereafter, she applied Rajuk for getting sale permission on the strength of the power of attorney but due to pendency of the case, she could not procure the same and, as such, she prayed for decreeing the suit by way of specific performance of contract in favour of the plaintiff.

6. Defendant Nos. 1-5 filed an application under Order VII, rule II (a) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating inter alia, that the defendant No. 18 executed registered agreement for sale on 19-11-2009 with the plaintiff in respect of the suit land and the period mentioned in the said agreement for sale is vague and unspecified and in fact no time is mentioned in the said agreement which is violation of section 54A of the Transfer of the Property Act. Another ground is that in a contract for sale of immovable property a time, to be effective from the date of registration, shall be mentioned. If no time is mentioned six months shall be deemed to be the time. Since no specific time has been mentioned in the agreement for sale dated 19-11-2009 for registration of deed of sale, 6 (six) months time is the time for registration of sale deed. According to the plaint, agreement for sale was executed on 19-11-2009 and the suit was filed on 30-7-2012 after long one year and six months which is barred under section :54A of the Transfer of Property Act and Article 113 of the Limitation Act.

7. The plaintiff contested the said application by filing written objection alleging inter alia, that the question of limitation raised by the defendants in their application is mixed question of law and facts which can be decided only by the trial court on taking evidence. He further stated that according to section, 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, time limit of six months for registration of the sale deed from the date of execution and registration of the agreement does not render the agreement void, as is declared void under section 53B of Transfer of Property Act. The said section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act does not put any bar to file the suit for specific performance of contract under section 12 of Specific Relief Act Hence section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act is not applicable to" the suit filed under section 12 of the Specific Relief Act. The defendant Nos. 1-5 executed power of attorney in favour of the defendant No. 18 and on the basis of the said power of attorney defendant No. 18 on 19-11-2009 executed registered agreement for sale in favour of the plaintiff and defendant No. 18 applied for sale permission to Rajuk but due to pendency of the suit, the same could not be procured. In the mean time, defendant Nos. 1-5 entered into agreement for sale of the suit property in favour of the defendant No. 6 and, as such, the defendant Nos. 1-5 committed fraud with him and prayed for rejection of the said application.

8. After hearing the aforesaid application, the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka on 4-7-2013 allowed the application and consequently rejected the plaint holding that the suit is barred by section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act and the Article 113 of the Limitation Act.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiff filed the aforesaid appeal before this Court.

10. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, has submitted that there are as many as 4(four) agreements for sale between the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1-5 dated 7-7-1987, 4-8-1989, 4-10-2009 and 19-1-2009 respectively with stipulation that the agreement will remain in force till the sale permission from Rajuk will be obtained; Rajuk due to pendency of Civil Appeal No. 201 of 2009 and 202 of 2009 before the Appellant Division did not accord sale permission as mentioned in the agreement, rejection of plaint on the ground of limitation is misconceived being contrary to the agreement and the law. In support of his submission he cited the case of Rojasara Ramjibhai Dahyabhai vs Jani reported in AIR 1986 SC 1912.

11. He has further submitted that the trial court erred in law in relying on section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act in computing the period of limitation for filing the suit which, in fact, will be guided by second part of Article 113 of the Limitation Act. In support of his submission he cited the case of Mahua Khair vs Amena Begum Ali Ispahani reported in 17 MLR (AD) 172 = 17 BLC (AD) 139.

12. By citing a case of Abul Khair (Md) vs Pubali Bank Ltd., 53 DLR (AD) 62, he has also submitted that the Court while deciding the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of plaint is not permitted by law to travel beyond the averments made in the plaint.

13. He has further submitted that the cause of action arose on 23-5-2012 when the plaintiff got certified copy of the registered sale agreement dated 9-5-2012 in favour of defendant No.6, which is very much within the prescribed period of limitation. The trial court erred in law in not considering the aforesaid facts and erroneously held that the suit is barred by limitation.

14. Mr Bhuiyan has lastly submitted that the suit being specific performance of contract and, the plaint was rejected on the point of limitation which is a mixed question of law and facts, is required to be decided upon taking evidence but the learned Joint District Judge erred in law in rejecting the plaint without taking evidence which is bad in law. In support of his contention he cited the cases of Abdul Malek Sawdagar vs Md Mahbubey Alam reported in 57 DLR (AD) 18, Mahbubul Haque (Md) vs Md A Kader Munshi reported in 52 DLR (AD) 49, and Shahabuddin (Md) vs Habibur Rahman reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99.

15. Mr Quamrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate on behalf of the appellant, in addition to the submissions of Mr Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, has enlightened us with the submission as to when the agreement for sale is contingent contract.

16. By referring section 62 of the Contract Act, he has further submitted that there are 4(four) contracts executed between the parties and on 19-11-2009 final agreement was executed and registered to meet the enhanced price of the property, so there is a novation of contract which the defendant Nos. 1-5 are bound to perform and as such prays for allowing the appeal.

17. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondents, by referring section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, has submitted that since the agreement for sale dated 19-11-2009 contains no specific time for registration of sale deed, 6 (six) months time is the time limit for registration of sale deed.

18. He has further submitted that according to Article 113 of the Limitation Act the time for filing a suit for specific performance of contract is one year i.e. the appellant had to file the suit within one and half year from the date of execution of the agreement for sale. Taking us to the record he has submitted that the contract was executed on 19-11-2009 and instant suit was filed on 30-7-2011 long after one year and six months which is barred by law of limitation. Considering this aspect of the case the trial court rightly rejected the plaint and, as such, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

19. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate for the respondents in addition to the submissions of Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate, has submitted that the suit is for specific performance of contract, as per section 21 (c) of the Specific Relief Act, where the court cannot find reasonable certainty of the term of the contract in that event the contract cannot be specifically enforced. In support of his contention he cited case of HN Fabrics Ltd. Vs Mallick Textile Industries reported in 37 DLR (AD) 126.

20. He has further submitted that the power of attorney executed by the defendant Nos. 1-5 in favour of the defendant No. 18 was revoked on 29-7-2010 which was to be treated as refusal to perform the contract and from that date limitation to file the suit would run.

21. By referring clauses 22 and 24 of the lease deed executed by the DIT now Rajuk, he has also submitted that the lease deed stipulates that all transfer of the property if not registered in the office of the lessor, the lessor will not be bound to recognize or accept any person as lessee of the property in place of transferor. In support of his submission he cited a case of AKM Amjad Hossain vs Md Nasir, reported in 7 BLC (AD) 101.

22. He has further submitted that without cancelling the 3rd contract executed by defendant No. 18 in favour of the plaintiff on 4-10-2009, the defendant No. 18 entered into another contract with the plaintiff on 19-11-2009 which was contrary to section 53B of the Transfer of the Property Act and on the basis of the said contract the plaintiff instituted the suit which is not maintainable and, as such, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

23. He has lastly submitted that according to section 53B of the Transfer of Property Act no immovable property under a contract for sale shall be transferred except to the vendee so long the contract subsists, unless the contract is lawfully rescinded, and any transfer made otherwise shall be void. In the present case the power of attorney holder without rescinding the 3rd contract subsisting with the plaintiff, she entered into 4th contract with the plaintiff on 19-11-2009 which is impugned contract and as such said contract dated 19-11-2009 is void.

24. The main contention of the defendant Nos. 1-5 as stated in their application for rejection of the plaint is that according to section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, since the agreement for sale did not specify any time limit for registration of sale deed, 6(six) months time is to be treated as the time limit for registration of sale deed and as per Article 113 of the limitation Act which stipulates one year time for filing suit, the suit was required to be filed within 6 (six) months + 1 (one) year = 11/2  (one and half) year. As the suit was filed beyond this period of one and half year, the plaint is liable to be rejected. The trial court also considering this argument rejected the plaint.

25. The terms of the agreement dated 19-11-2009 are as follows:

"অদ্য রোজ হাজিরান মজলিশে নিম্নে স্বাক্ষরকারীগনের মোকাবিলায় অত্র দলিলদা তা-দাত্রীগনের পক্ষে নিযুক্তীয় আমি অত্র দলিল সস্পাদকারিনী আপনি অত্র বায়নানামা দলিল গ্রহিতার/ ক্রেতার নিকট হইতে বায়না বাবদ অগ্রিম মূল্য ১.০০,০০,০০০ টাকা মাত্র নগদ একযোগে হাতে হাতে বুঝিয়া পাইয়া অনিয়া এই মর্মে স্বীকার ও অস্বীকার করিতেছি যে, রাজধানী উন্নয়ন (রাজউক) হইতে বিক্রয়/হস্তান্তর অনুমতি প্রদানের পর হইতে আগামী ৩(তিন) মাস মেয়াদের মধ্যে মূল্যের অবশিষ্ট মূল্য ১,২০,০০,০০০ (এক কোটি বিশ লক্ষ) টাকা মাত্র বুঝিয়া পাইয়া অনিয়া আপনি অত্র বায়নানামা দলিল গ্রহিতার বরাবর নিম্ন তফসিল বর্ণিত প্লটের এক বা একাধিক সাফ কবলা দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করিয়া দিব বা দিতে

বাধ্য রহিলাম।"

26. In that agreement it is further staled that:

"পরবর্তীতে উক্ত ১১৩৬৩ নং বায়নানামা দলিলের মেয়াদ পূর্ণ হয় অথ্যাৎ বায়নানামা দলিলের মেয়াদ অতিবাহিত হয়ে গেছে বিধায় নিন্ম তফসিল বর্ণিত প্লটের সম্পতি অত্র বায়নানামা দলিল দ্বারা আপনি অত্র বয়নানামা দলিল গ্রহিতার সহিত বায়নাপত্রে অবদ্ধ হইয়া সাবেক ডি আই টি (ঢাকা ইম্প্রভমেন্ট ট্রাষ্ট) বর্তমানে রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ হইতে হস্তান্ত/বিক্রয় অনুমতি সহ রাজউক কর্তৃপক্ষের অন্যান্য যাবতীয় কার্যাদি সম্পূর্ণ করার পর আপনি অত্র

বায়নানামা দলিল গ্রহিতার বরা���র হস্তান্তর/সাফ কবলা দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করিয়া দেওয়া পর্যন্ত অত্র বায়নানামা দলিলের কার্যকারিতার বলবৎ থাকিবে।"

27. From aforesaid terms of the agreement for sale it is clear that a specific time, that is after obtaining sale permission from Rajuk to be effective from the date of registration, was mentioned for execution and registration of the instrument of the sale; as the contingency did not happen, the question of limitation does not arise.

28. The cancellation of power of attorney has no nexus with the agreement for sale, which is not yet cancelled by the defendants. In the meantime defendant No. 18 filed a suit against the revocation of the power of attorney which is still pending. During subsistent of the agreement with the plaintiff when defendant Nos. 1-5 entered into a fresh contract with defendant No. 6 the plaintiff got notice of it on 23-5-2012 that the performance is refused by the defendant Nos. 1-5 and within one year from that date, on 30-7-2012, filed the suit which is very much within the period of limitation.

29. The submission of the learned Advocate for the respondents to the effect that as per section 21(c) of the Specific Relief Act as the court did not find reasonable certainty of the term of the contract, the same cannot be specifically enforced has got little merit. The facts of the case reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 271 = 37 DLR (AD) 126, in short, are that:

"Plaintiff brought a suit for specific performance of contract alleging inter alia that the plaintiff entered into contract with principle defendant No.1 through defendant No.2 the managing partner for purchase of the suit property to which defendant 2 agreed to sell and price was settled at Taka 9,00,001. The plaintiff paid in cash 1,00,001 as earnest money and the deed of agreement for sale was exhibited on 9-1-1979 and it was stipulated that defendants would hand over possession of the suit property to the plaintiff on receipt of a further sum of Taka 4,00,000 out of the consideration money from the plaintiff by 30-4-1979 and on receipt of the balance consideration money by which time the defendants would obtain requisite permission from the authority and necessary income tax clearance certificate at their own costs. The plaintiff, however, could not pay the principal defendant further sum of Taka 4,00,000 as stipulated but the plaintiff was willing and ready to pay balance Taka 8,00,000 but the defendants did not pay heed to the same in spite of repeated request to complete the transaction and therefore suite specific performance of contract was filed. The defendant has admitted the case of the plaintiff that there was an agreement for sale and the earnest money of Taka 1,00,001 was paid but the price was fixed at Taka 16,00,001 and not at Taka 9,00,001.

…………………………………………………………………………………..

30. In the cited case the plaintiff produced Exhibit 1 as to the terms of the contract whereas the defendant produced Exhibit C and the prices in the two terms are completely different, PW 2 who drafted the agreement was examined and he himself stated:

"Exhibit 1 is not the same draft which I drafted as Exhibit 1 includes the boundary of the schedule which was not in my draft."

31.The High Court Division observed that:

"The plaintiff could not prove his case of terms of the deed of agreement; though the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree or specific performance of contract, and accordingly dismissed the suit with a direction to refund the Taka 1,00,001 to the plaintiff which was paid as earnest money."

32. Considering the cases of Hyam vs Cub bay AIR 1916 page 1 (FB); Rossiter vs Miller 1878,3 AC 1124, Hatzfeld Wildenburg vs Alexander 1912 1 Ch. 284-248 and AIR 1933 PC 31, the Appellate Division held that "the High Court Division took the correct view that there was no concluded contract which could be enforced by specific performance."

33. The facts of the case reported in 7 BLC (AD) 101 that the plaintiff had given a power of attorney to his uncle defendant No. 1 for running his business in the shop premises situated at Mohammadpur Kacha Bazar due to preoccupation elsewhere. The shop was allotted to the plaintiff by the defendant No.3, Deputy Commissioner, Housing and Settlement Directorate, for running grocery shop. "The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that the sale deed dated 26-10-1981 executed by the petitioner No.1 on the basis of power of attorney of the plaintiff described in the Schedule A to the plaint is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and' recovery of the khas possession of the shop No. 98 at Mohammdpur Kacha Bazar allotted by the defendant No.3 for running grocery shop. The plaintiff entrusted his uncle to look after and manage his business in the aforesaid shop and registered a power of attorney on 14-3-1981 for the said business. The plaintiff came to know that defendant No.1 has created fraudulent sale deed in favour of his wife defendant No.2 in respect of the suit shop by execution and registration of sale deed dated 26-10-1981. The plaintiff after getting the said information revoked the said power of attorney dated 14-3-1981 by a registered revocation deed dated 5-1-1984. It transpires that the defendant No.1 got a clause inserted in the power of attorney to the effect that he. could transfer of the shop room, the said clause is in violation of the terms and condition of the allotment and the plaintiff did not confer such power on the defendant No.1 Defendant No.3 has not yet been executed any title deed in favour of the plaintiff. The fraudulent insertion of clause as to transfer has been done subsequently and in violation of the terms and conditions of the allotment. There was no consideration for the said transfer in favour of the defendant No.2. The deed of sale executed by the defendant No.1 in favour of his wife defendant No.2 is also collusive and illegal and without any consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff.

………………………………………………………………………………………………………

34. The trial court decreed the suit and on appeal the suit was dismissed allowing the appeal. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment made the Rule absolute decreeing the suit.

35. The courts below believed the plaintiffs case of fraudulent insertion of the clause as to transfer in the power of attorney. Since no permission has ever been taken from proforma defendant No.3 for transfer of the shop premises allot- ted to the plaintiff and, as such, the power of attorney was not executed in accordance with law."

36. Considering this view our Appellate Division dismissed the petition.

<u>37. The submission of Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate, is that if we do not consider the amended section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act and the section 113 of the Limitation Act, the intention of the legislature will be frustrated. Mr Bhuiyan learned Advocate by citing 40 DLR (AD) 116 submits that court is not concerned with any presumed intention of the legislature its task is to get at the intention as expressed in the statute. We respectively agree with the aforesaid decision. The limitation prescribed for a suit for specific performance of contract, under Article 113 of the Limitation Act, is one year or if no such date is fixed, when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused from where the cause of action accrues. In the facts and circumstances of the present case the defendant Nos. 1-5 sold out the suit property through registered deed dated 9-5-2012 and plaintiff obtained certified copies of the said deed on 23-5-2012 and limitation till run when the plaintiff obtained certified copies of two registered sale agreements i.e. on 23-5-2012. It prima facie appears that the suit was filed within time which will be decided by the trial court on taking evidence.</u>

38. The submission of Mr Bhuiyan is that the agreement for sale dated 19-11-2009 between the panics was not a contingent contract within the meaning of section 31 of the Contract Act rather it was a concluded contract and, as such, the plaintiff is entitled for specific performance of contract. In support of his contention he cited a case of Balwant singh vs Raijaram reported in AIR 1975 Rajasthan 73.

39. In the case reported in 57 DLR (AD) 18 their Lordships held that:

"The question as to whether the plaint is liable to be rejected being barred by law must be apparent from the statement made in the plaint itself and not from the written statement or any other material other than that has been put in the plaint. Thus this provision applies when it appears from the statement in the plaint that suit is barred by any law either due to limitation, res-judicata or barred by law providing ouster of the jurisdiction of the Court."

<u>40. In the cases reported in 52 DLR (AD) 48, 13 BLD (AD) 217 and 50 DLR (AD) 99 their Lordships held that the question of limitation being a mixed question of law and facts, should be decided at the time of trial on taking evidence.</u>

<u>41. The defendant Nos. 1-5 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 (a) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the plaint does not disclose any cause of action. A plaint may be rejected for non-disclosure of any cause of action. There is difference between the following two expressions (i) the plaint does not disclose any cause of action and (ii) the plaintiff has no cause of action. The first expression implies that in the plaint itself no cause of action has been disclosed. The second expression means that a cause Of action has been disclosed in the plaint by the plaintiff but on evidence it is found that he has no cause of action. So, a plaint can be rejected only when the plaint does not disclose any cause of action. But if it discloses a cause of action, then the questions whether that cause of action was actually present, whether it was sufficient to file the suit etc. being question of fact cannot be decided at the initial stage and can be decided only on the basis of evidence at the time of trial and for deciding those questions, an issue is to be framed.</u>

42. Whether the plaint discloses a cause of action is to be ascertained by reading the whole plaint, cause of action may not be a single cause, it may be a bundle of facts, as found by their lordships in 2004 BCR (AD) 138, 56 DLR(AD) 210. Cause of action consists of the entire set of facts which gives rise to a legal action and is to be proved by the plaintiff in order to succeed in the suit, as found in 2 MLR (AD) 28 = 2 BLC (AD) 47 and 49 DLR (AD) 99. But, if after perusing the entire plaint, it is found that no cause of action has been disclosed, the plaint must be rejected.

<u>43. A plaint may be rejected by the Court by invoking its inherent power even the provisions of Order VII, rule 11 are found not to be applicable. It is now a settled principle of law that if the continuation of the suit is found to be an abuse of the process of the Court, if the suit is foredoomed or if the ultimate result of the suit is as clear as the daylight, the suit should be buried at its inception by rejecting the plaint by invoking inherent powers of the Court provided section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, this principle is laid down in the case reported in 53 DLR (AD) 12, 24 BLD (AD) 223.</u>

44. The submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent is that lessee shall not sell, charge, mortgage, exchange, the suit property without prior permission from Rajuk lessor; the power of attorney was not duly authorized by the Rajuk which was revoked by registered revocation deed No. 8427 dated 29-7-2010 and, as such, continuation of the present suit is nothing but a fruitless litigation. In the present case, the defendants entered into an agreement for sale of the suit plot with the plaintiff and the plaintiff instituted the present suit against the defendants for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of suit plot by invoking section 12 of the Specific Performance of Contract and the defendant No. 18, power of attorney holder, filed Writ Petition- No. 6360 of 2010 before the High Court Division against the Rajuk and others for getting sale permission in respect of the suit land and defendant No. 18 also filed Title Suit No. 94 of 2011 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for declaration challenging the deed of revocation of power of attorney against the defendant Nos. 1-5, which are pending before the Court. On perusal of the facts of the case reported in 53 DLR (AD) 12 we cannot hold that the ultimate result of the suit is as clear as daylight. So the facts of the reported case are distinguishable from the facts of the present case.

45. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case, we find little merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the respondents and the decisions cited by them are not applicable in the facts of the present case.

46. We find substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the appellant and find merit in the appeal.

47. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

48. The judgment and decree dated 4-7-2013 (decree signed on 8-7-2013) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 838 of 2012 rejecting the plaint is hereby set-aside. Trial court is directed to proceed with the suit as per law.

Send down the lower Court's records at once.

Communicate the order.

End.
